overview: Matamba was an existing kingdom when Njinga took power around 1630. It became a refuge for displaced people and a major inland trading power, with a history that continued beyond her lifetime.

items.text: Women ruled Matamba before Njinga. Her takeover displaced central authority while retaining the previous ruling family in local power.
People of different origins sought refuge in Njinga’s realm. Military organization helped incorporate newcomers, under conditions shaped by regional violence.
Matamba linked the interior with Atlantic commerce. Njinga resisted Portuguese encroachment while participating in the sale of captives.
Capuchin mediation helped negotiations in the 1650s. Njinga’s later Catholic practice accompanied changes to court policy.

sources.title: Mariana Bracks Fonseca, Queen Njinga of Ndongo and Matamba (2022)
Alexander Ives Bortolot, Ana Nzinga, Queen of Ndongo (2003)
